note: Claims ledger for the Evaluation Lab. Verdicts are limited to the stored runs named below. 'unverified' means this lab did not measure it; it does not mean the claim is false.

claims.evidence: Live validation: 4/4 attack runs detected and contained; median MTTC 48 ms, p95 312 ms; median MTTD 1 ms. This is a simulator measurement, not a production latency guarantee.
claims.action: Keep the README wording scoped to measured simulator runs.

claims.claim: Benign compressed formats (.zip, .jpg, .png, .docx) produce zero false positives.
claims.evidence: 0 false-positive traces across 162 held-out traces (95% CI upper bound 2.3%) and 0/4 benign live simulator runs. Zero observed is not proof of zero.
claims.action: README must say 'no false positives observed in the evaluation set', not 'zero false positives'.

claims.claim: Swarm correlation catches >= 3 distinct principals within a 120-second window.
claims.evidence: Shipped data/policies.yaml uses min_principals: 2, window_seconds: 60, flagged_writes: 12. The README claim does not match the shipped configuration.
claims.action: README corrected to 2 principals / 60 seconds / 12 flagged writes.

claims.evidence: The public storage API path produced 2-principal activity; the product detected and contained it. The incident was raised before cross-principal correlation was the deciding signal, so the correlation component itself is not isolated by this run.
claims.action: Report detection separately from the attribution of the deciding signal.

claims.claim: Cross-principal swarm correlation is the deciding detection signal for multi-principal attacks.
claims.evidence: Both live swarm runs were detected and contained, but incident.isSwarm was false in both: the product raised the incident through other signals before correlation was the deciding factor. The replay ablation D9d (swarm correlation disabled) also detected 100% of held-out attack traces.
claims.action: Do not claim the swarm-correlation component is load-bearing based on this run.

claims.evidence: D9a (canaries removed) detected 100% of held-out attack traces, identical to D9. Entropy/magic signals carried the detection in this trace set. The canary ablation did not lower detection.
claims.action: Do not claim canaries are load-bearing based on this benchmark; report the null ablation.

claims.claim: Control-plane hard triggers add detection value.
claims.evidence: D9b (control-plane triggers removed) detected 100% of held-out attack traces, identical to D9.
claims.action: Report the null ablation; do not attribute the headline result to these triggers.

claims.claim: Entropy and magic-byte inspection are load-bearing detection signals.
claims.evidence: D9c (entropy/magic neutralised) fell from 100% to 71.4% detection across 162 held-out traces (McNemar p < 0.001 in the ransomware family).
claims.action: Keep this claim, with the stored run cited.

claims.claim: 1-Click Restore restores objects bit-for-bit from the vault.
claims.evidence: Recovery verification scenario passed its SHA-256 assertion (100% match) in live validation.
claims.action: Scope the claim to the local simulator and the shipped vault adapter.

claims.claim: The isolated WORM vault guarantees durable, credential-isolated recovery.
claims.evidence: The local adapter models an isolated vault. No external Backblaze B2 or MinIO Object Lock bucket was exercised. Free-tier hosts may sleep or lose data.
claims.action: README must not claim durability on free-tier hosting; add the provider caveat.

claims.claim: Supabase Storage S3 can serve as a vault/restore target.
claims.evidence: Supabase Storage S3 does not provide S3 Object Lock or versioning semantics required by the vault and version-purge defenses. It can be a monitored source, not a WORM vault target.
claims.action: README corrected: Supabase is a monitored source, not a vault or versioning target.

claims.evidence: The server reads x-defyswarm-role from the request header and defaults to admin. Any client can set it. This is a demo role switch, not authentication or authorization.
claims.action: README corrected: the role header is a client-supplied demo control, not authentication.

claims.claim: The operator audit log is immutable.
claims.evidence: The audit log is an append-only array persisted in data/ledger.json. It is not tamper-evident and can be edited by anyone with filesystem access.
claims.action: README corrected: append-only local ledger, not tamper-proof.

claims.claim: Out-of-band operation preserves zero-latency read/write performance.
claims.evidence: The lab measured no application data-path latency. Detection is asynchronous in the simulator, but no production load test was run.
claims.action: Do not present zero-latency as a measured result.

claims.claim: Quota-safe 64 KB range sampling inspects content and cryptographic signals.
claims.evidence: The replay traces carry entropy and magic-byte fields directly. The live simulator uses the local adapter. No external S3 range-sampling call was measured.
claims.action: Keep as a design statement, not an evaluated result.

claims.claim: AI evasion audits test adaptive canary robustness.
claims.evidence: No Groq API key was used and no classifier audit was run in this evaluation.
claims.action: Do not cite the evaluation lab as evidence for AI classifier performance.

claims.evidence: D9 detected 100% [96.7%, 100%] of 112 held-out attack traces vs D4 53.6%, D8 53.6%, D3 58.9%; D9 median files lost 1 vs 18 for D3 and 6 for D8. Baselines are reference implementations, not vendor products.
claims.action: Always state that baselines are reference implementations and that traces are synthetic replay.
